variants.headline: Looking back: builder signs for a new project
variants.sub: A construction contract for {project} has been awarded to {builder}.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: The builder {builder} had signed a contract for {project}.

The gazette records the builder, the project and the price as the terms established by the award. A signed construction contract and a completed project require separate notices. The public record should preserve that sequence rather than describe the agreement as though it had already produced the promised building.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The handling of {target} should be assessed against the signed undertaking. This paper records the award and agreed price without announcing a construction result that the contract itself has not yet delivered.

variants.headline: Looking back: a price agreed, a building still to deliver
variants.sub: The company {builder} has won the building contract for {project}.
variants.body:
Looking back to our earlier coverage, this was the news: A construction contract for {project} had been awarded to {builder}.

The gazette records the builder, the project and the price as the terms established by the award. A signed construction contract and a completed project require separate notices. The public record should preserve that sequence rather than describe the agreement as though it had already produced the promised building.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

variants.body:

Changes since then deserve examination against the original record. The need to distinguish an established event from its associated hopes and fears remains.
